children: By Mike Scarcella

Washington lawyer Tom Goldstein on Wednesday failed to convince a US appeals court to free him from jail as he fights to overturn his conviction and six-year prison sentence for tax and financial crimes stemming from his side career as a high-stakes poker player.
In a brief order, the Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals denied Goldstein's request to be released from custody.

Goldstein, once one of the country’s top lawyers arguing cases before the US Supreme Court, was sentenced in July following his conviction over allegations that he failed to report millions of dollars in poker winnings, lied on home mortgage loan documents and made improper payments through his former law firm.
US District Judge Lydia Griggsby in the federal court in Greenbelt, Maryland, had allowed Goldstein to remain free during his trial but ordered him to begin serving his prison sentence immediately.
Goldstein's lawyers and the US Attorney's Office for Maryland did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In a court filing, prosecutors called Goldstein "a flight risk with substantial international ties, including with a foreign billionaire who, in Goldstein’s view, is indebted to Goldstein for his own freedom." His lawyers countered that he has no intention of fleeing if released.

Goldstein has argued Griggsby's instructions to jurors at the trial violated due ​process and “⁠crippled” his defense strategy. He also argues that the trial court wrongly excluded some of his communication with third parties that he said contained evidence countering the government's assertion that he acted willfully to violate tax laws.
In a
, his lawyers told the appeals court that "in this case, the government decided to secure a conviction no matter the facts or law."
Goldstein argued more than 40 cases ​at the Supreme Court before retiring in 2023 and was a founder of the SCOTUSblog legal news website.
He was charged in January 2025 with concealing earnings and losses from poker games in the United States and abroad with stakes reaching millions of dollars.
A jury convicted Goldstein in February after a six-week trial. He admitted at trial that he should have paid more attention to his tax returns but ​denied intentionally violating any laws.
The case is United States v. Goldstein, 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 26-4392.
For the United States: David Bornstein and Jason Poole of the Department of Justice
For Goldstein: Elizabeth Prelogar of Cooley; and Jonathan Kravis of Liu Shur Kravis
